title: the Samkhya Karika)
hook: two travelers left behind in a forest, one who can't walk and one who can't see

segments.voice: Yesterday the Samkhya Karika argued that the effect is already in its cause: yogurt in the milk, oil in the sesame.

A caravan has been scattered in a forest, and two travelers are left behind. One can't walk. The other can't see. Night is coming. The one who can't walk can see the path, the river, the way out, but he can't take a step. The one who can't see has strong legs and a strong back, but he has no idea which way to go. Alone, both of them stay in the forest. The classic commentaries on the Samkhya Karika tell this little story, and the Karika itself names it in a single phrase. Today it explains how the whole world got moving.
screen: `A CARAVAN SCATTERED.` → `ONE CAN'T WALK, ONE CAN'T SEE.` → `ALONE, BOTH STAY LOST.`

segments.voice: Here's the ending. The traveler who can't see lifts the other onto his shoulders. Now one does the walking and the other does the seeing, and together they get out of the forest. Once they reach the village, they go their separate ways. The Karika uses this picture for the two from Samkhya's opening days. Prakriti is the one with legs: she moves, changes and unfolds, but she has no seeing of her own. Purusha is the one with eyes: the witness, who sees but never acts. Their coming together, the verse says, is like the lame and the blind, and creation unfolds from that meeting. And the Karika says what the meeting is for. It's so that purusha can see prakriti, and so that purusha can finally be set free. In Samkhya the world isn't an accident, and it isn't a trap someone built. The whole unfolding, the gunas, the I-maker, the senses, the elements, is a journey with a purpose, and the purpose is seeing clearly. Notice too how the story ends. The two travelers part ways. That's where Samkhya is heading, and the next two days get there. Not everyone in the Hindu tradition tells the end of the journey this way. Vedanta, at the close of this season, has its own account. For now, the picture is enough. A partnership that neither side could manage alone, that gets somewhere, and then lets go.
screen: `ONE CARRIES, ONE GUIDES.` · `PRAKRITI MOVES, PURUSHA SEES.` · `A MEETING WITH A PURPOSE.` · `THE TRAVELERS PART WAYS.`

segments.voice: Rest one hand on your knee, lift it a little and lower it again, a few times: the hand is the one with legs, and it moves. Then notice the seeing, aware of the movement without lifting anything, and let the hand go still: let the body carry, let the seeing see. If you pray, you can offer thanks for the body that carries you.
The Samkhya Karika. Its picture of the world's beginning: prakriti, who moves but can't see, and purusha, who sees but can't move, getting out of the forest together.
Your line: the Samkhya Karika. One carries, one guides, and together they get out. Day one thousand one hundred seventy-eight.
